source_locators.claim: 纳入判断依据：目标是研究而非通用产品应用。
source_locators.quote_or_summary: Command-line coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Gemini CLI) can already read and write files and sustain long sessions, yet end-to-end research still fragments across chat tools, IDEs, terminals, and writing environments, and the decisions that make it auditable are rarely preserved.

source_locators.claim: 科学对象或研究任务由正文明确指出。
source_locators.quote_or_summary: instruction (“conduct a rigorous, publication-quality study…”) across three medical problems:

source_locators.claim: 方法包含任务路由、执行和结果处理。

source_locators.quote_or_summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) provides an established setting for quantum control and computation 19, including experimental polynomial optimization on a four-qubit processor 20. Here we evaluate an agent-assisted experimental strategy on five three-qubit NMR processors, using three-qubit Grover target-state preparation as a common experimental task 21, 22. The processors shared a common experimental interface but differed in Hamiltonian parameters, spectral structure and operating conditions. The strategy was developed under human supervision on one processor and applied sequentially to four others. Each deployment involved local calibrat

In T2E, the agent invokes and coordinates deterministic tools to characterize the processor, synthesize controls, acquire measurements and reconstruct experimental outputs. It uses the resulting evidence to select subsequent actions and adapt the experimental procedure. Operators retain responsibility for instrument preparation, physical adjustment, safety and procedural authorization. The agent therefore coordinates decisions at a higher level than a conventional controller, while numerical calculations remain assigned to deterministic tools and physical interventions to operators.

Progress in quantum hardware requires a growing volume of experiments across diverse devices, straining the capacity of human experts. Automation remains challenging because device differences and drift can render workflows developed on one processor unsuitable for another. Here we present an agent-assisted experimental strategy for conducting experiments across three-qubit nuclear magnetic resonance processors. The benchmark contains ten algorithms from Lan’s monograph (Lan, 2020) (FOML) and five research-paper algorithms: AMSGrad, STORM, SPIDER, PAGE, and Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM). The research-paper tasks cover online regret bounds, convergence guarantees for stochastic and finite-sum nonconvex optimization, and PAC-Bayes generalization bounds.

source_locators.quote_or_summary: We present an AI-assisted Lean 4 formalization of the Poincaré conjecture. The project began with limited reusable formal infrastructure for the geometric analysis behind the proof. To organize this work, we combined a proof blueprint prepa

and restarted the main formalization in September with about 90 milestones, each specifying the definitions and Lean statement required for its target. The milestones provided shared mathematical targets, exposed dependencies, and made progress and blockers visible. The engineers used this structure to coordinate parallel agent work, while mathematicians reviewed the final theorem and key intermediate statements and helped resolve mathematical difficulties during proof construction.

By late July, we had completed a Lean formalization of the Hopf–Rinow theorem and reviewed its mathematical correctness. After an initial attempt with an AI system failed, a mathematician reorganized the proof into a clearer route, enabling the system to complete the development. Throughout August, we continued formalizing foundational material from these sources and completed a natural-language blueprint of the Poincaré proof following Morgan–Tian.

records.title: Beyond Equation Search: Conjecture-Guided Discovery with SCOPE and ClosureBench

changes.reason: Direct synonym normalization, supported by the existing Note. This proposal does not remove additional unknown owner labels.

source_locators.quote_or_summary: Most symbolic regression methods optimize candidate equations, but improving an equation’s fit does not establish whether its underlying scientific conjecture should be retained, revised, or rejected.

After initial data analysis and literature review, each scientist formulates a structured conjecture containing a natural-language explanation, variable relationships, testable predictions, and candidate equation space.

Evaluating scientific discovery requires assessing not only the derived equations, but also the discovery process: how evidence is acquired and whether it supports the agent’s conclusions. We introduce ClosureBench, an interactive benchmark containing 60 closure-discovery tasks across five scientific domains. Each task embeds an unknown algebraic relation in a known PDE system. An OpenFOAM interface supports experimental evidence acquisition, while evaluation measures equation accuracy, identified scientific properties, evidential support, and improvement through interactive research.
